subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs, model topology
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@finserve.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T17:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap + next steps — technical deep-dive (latency/throughput SLOs)

Hi Amit,

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful to see FinServe's expected traffic patterns and the hard SLOs you're trying to meet. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned.

Key pain points you raised:
- 95th percentile p50 latency requirement: 300ms for single-turn generative responses (average prompt ~150 tokens).
- Peak QPS: expected burst to 400 r/s for short periods (approx 10-15 minutes) with steady-state 80 r/s.
- Deterministic throughput for batch jobs (off-peak embedding pipelines) with predictable cost.
- Data residency + audit logging requirements for customer PII handled by the model.

What we discussed we can deliver (high level):
- Dedicated deployment topology: 2x dedicated GPU pools in us-west with cross-region fallback to us-east for DR.
- Model profile: 13B Llama-style model quantized (4-bit) for gen workloads; we suggested a compute test to validate latency at 150-token responses.
- Batching & KV cache: enable small-window continuous batching with prefix caching to reduce per-token cost without violating tail latency.

Action items / next steps:
1) Marissa to scope an in-house latency test (target: 95p <= 300ms at 80 r/s, graceful degradation at 400 r/s). Marissa, can you confirm estimated infra and time?
2) Aditya to share SLO summary + network topology diagram (attached).
3) Amit to share representative prompt set + expected token distributions and the compliance contact for audit logging requirements.

Attachments: 2026-08-04-slo-summary.pdf (SLO summary + test plan), network-topology.png.

If anything above is inaccurate or missing, please flag. Otherwise, I'll schedule the infra test for next week and loop in engineering.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Thanks Aditya — this matches our conversation. A few clarifications: 

- The 300ms target is strict for our customer-facing product (95th percentile), but we can tolerate up to 600ms for backup/DR in cross-region failover.
- Token distribution: ~60% responses under 120 tokens, 30% 120-400 tokens, 10% long-form >400 tokens (these long-form requests are typically batch-processed at night).
- For compliance, please send any logging retention options and whether you can forward logs to our SIEM. Our compliance lead is Priya Natarajan (priya.n@finserve.com).

We'll pull together a sample prompt set and share by EOD Friday. Also, please note the procurement team expects an initial POC contract (1 mo) before committing to Dedicated.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

– Amit

Hi all,

Thanks for the details, Amit. A few technical notes and a proposed test plan so the POC validates the right things: 

Summary of constraints we need to validate
- Latency target: 95p <= 300ms @ 80 r/s (steady); tail behavior at 400 r/s bursts.
- Payloads: use the token distribution Amit provided; we should run three buckets (short/medium/long) and weight traffic accordingly.
- Model: we'll run two variants for the POC — a 13B quantized variant (faster, lower cost) and a 33B float16 baseline for quality comparison.

Proposed POC test plan (2 weeks):
1) Infra provisioning (Day 1): spin up dedicated GPU pool (2 nodes) in us-west with autoscale disabled for deterministic tests.
2) Baseline latency run (Day 2): single-client load to verify median/95p at low QPS. Collect token-level timings and KV cache hit rates.
3) Burst test (Day 3): synthetic bursts to 400 r/s for 15 minutes; verify degradation policy and fallback to lower-latency model variant.
4) Batch embedding run (Day 4): run scheduled offline pipeline to validate throughput and quantization accuracy.
5) Observability + logs (Days 2-5): forward audit logs (per request id) to FinServe SIEM endpoint; test retention options (30/90/365 days).

Network/topology notes
- We recommend colocating the KG/DB layer and inference pool in the same VPC to avoid cross-VPC hops. If FinServe wants SAAS mode, we'll enable VPC peering and a private link to restrict egress.
- Expected egress: ~1-2MB/s per 100 r/s depending on response size; we can provide exact numbers after we run the token-weighted test.

Data & compliance
- We can support forwarding request/response logs to your SIEM and offer a customer-managed KMS for keying at rest. We also have SOC 2 audit artifacts we can share during the procurement review.

Deliverables for the POC
- Test harness (scripts and load curves)
- SLO report (latency percentiles, token-level breakdown, KV cache effectiveness)
- Cost estimate for steady-state and peak scenarios

I'll plan to have an initial infra estimate and test scripts by EOD Monday. Aditya — once Amit shares the prompt set and Priya's compliance contact, we'll start the SIEM integration test.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Systems Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
